standards.name: Real-time PCR Data Markup Language (RDML)
standards.abstract: The Real-time PCR Data Markup Language (RDML) is a structured, XML-based data standard for exchanging quantitative PCR (qPCR) (and later digital PCR) data. It captures raw fluorescence time-series (amplification and melting curves) and structured metadata describing experiments, runs, reactions (wells), samples, targets, dyes, thermal cycling conditions, experimenters and software, so files enable re-analysis and interpretation. RDML is maintained by the international RDML Consortium and distributed with a formal XML Schema (XSD), reference implementations (RDML-Python, RDML-Tools, RDML R package) and validators; it addresses the need for a universal, machine-readable exchange format to allow instrument software, analysis tools, collaborators, journals and readers to share annotated qPCR data reproducibly.

classification.rationale: The source material is an XML Schema (XSD) and detailed reference documentation that defines named elements and complex types with explicit data types (e.g. xs:float, xs:string, enumerations). This is genuine field-level structure (a metadata table/schema), not prose guidance or an ordered workflow, so the correct classification is 'table'.

rdml_file_rdml_data_xml.name: rdml_data.xml (file placement rule)
rdml_file_rdml_data_xml.descr: The XML file containing the RDML compliant data must be stored in a file named rdml_data.xml and optionally compressed into an archive with .rdml or .rdm extension; archives must contain only that single file.
rdml_file_rdml_data_xml.evidence: The xml file containing the RDML compliant data should be stored in a file named rdml_data.xml. This file should be compressed using pkzip compatible compression into an archive. The archive can have any name, but instead of having the extension .zip it should have the extension .rdml (preferably) or .rdm. Archives ending in .rdml or .rdm should only contain one file, the file rdml_data.xml.

file_encoding_newline_decimal.name: XML encoding / newline / decimal separator
file_encoding_newline_decimal.descr: Advice for the XML file encoding and character conventions: UTF-8, newline as \n, decimal separator as point '.'
file_encoding_newline_decimal.evidence: The XML file should be encoded in UTF-8, \n should be used as newline character and a point "." as decimal separator.

rdml_id.publisher.name: rdml id - publisher
rdml_id.publisher.descr: Publisher string assigned to the RDML file identifier element (rdmlIdType.publisher).
rdml_id.publisher.evidence: This element can be used to assign a publisher and id to the RDML file.

rdml_id.serialNumber.name: rdml id - serialNumber
rdml_id.serialNumber.descr: Serial number string assigned to the RDML file identifier element (rdmlIdType.serialNumber).
rdml_id.serialNumber.evidence: This element can be used to assign a publisher and id to the RDML file.

experimenter.name: experimenter (contact details)
experimenter.descr: Contact details of the experimenter (firstName, lastName, email, labName, labAddress) stored as experimenterType.
experimenter.type: object (experimenter: {id, firstName, lastName, email?, labName?, labAddress?})
experimenter.evidence: Contact details of the experimenter. Inherits: rdmlBaseType. Fields: id, firstName, lastName, email, labName, labAddress.

documentation.text.name: documentation
documentation.text.descr: Reusable textual documentation elements that can be referenced by samples, targets or experiments (documentationType.text with required id attribute).
documentation.text.evidence: These elements should be used if the same description applies to many samples, targets or experiments.

raw_full_info.source: artifact0 / artifact20 (documentationType complexType in XSD) and RDML docs

dye.id.name: dye.id
dye.id.descr: Identifier for a fluorescent dye used by targets; dye entries hold an id and description.
dye.id.evidence: dye - information about a dye. Detailed information about the dye. Inherits: rdmlBaseType. Fields: id, description.

sample.id.name: sample.id
sample.id.descr: Sample identifier referencing a defined template solution (sampleType). Samples can carry quantities and annotations.
sample.id.evidence: A "samples" is a defined template solution. Dilutions of the same material differ in concentration and are considered different samples. A technical replicate samples should contain the same name (reactions are performed on the same material), and biological replicates should contain different names (the nucleic acids derived from the different biological replicates are not the same).

target.id.name: target.id
target.id.descr: Target identifier representing a defined PCR reaction; targets include sequences, dye references, efficiency metadata and optional commercialAssay metadata.
target.id.evidence: A target is a defined PCR reaction. PCR reactions for the same gene which differ in primer sequences are considered different targets.

cqDetectionMethod.name: cqDetectionMethod
cqDetectionMethod.descr: Method used to determine the Cq value (an enumerated controlled vocabulary).
cqDetectionMethod.evidence: The method used to determine the Cq value. (enumerations shown in XSD)\n... <xs:enumeration value="automated threshold and baseline settings"/> <xs:enumeration value="manual threshold and baseline settings"/> <xs:enumeration value="second derivative maximum"/> <xs:enumeration value="other"/>

data.tar.name: data.tar (target reference)
data.tar.descr: TargetID - a reference to a target for a particular reaction data entry (idReferencesType).
data.tar.evidence: TargetID - A reference to a target.

data.cq.name: data.cq (Cq / quantification cycle)
data.cq.descr: Quantification cycle (Cq) — the calculated fractional PCR cycle used for downstream quantification. Special negative values indicate 'Not Available'.
data.cq.evidence: Quantification cycle - The calculated fractional PCR cycle used for downstream quantification. Negative values are used to express following conditions: Not Available: -1.0

data.excl.name: data.excl (excluded flag / reason)
data.excl.descr: Optional string present if an entry should not be evaluated; may contain explanation(s). Multiple reasons separated by semicolons.
data.excl.evidence: Excluded - Present if this entry should not be evaluated. It may contain a string with reason for exclusion. Several reasons for exclusion should be separated by semicolons ";".

data.adp.cyc.name: adp.cyc (amplification data point: cycle)
data.adp.cyc.descr: Cycle number at which an amplification data point was measured (part of dpAmpCurveType).
data.adp.cyc.evidence: Cycle - The PCR cycle at which data point was collected.

data.adp.tmp.name: adp.tmp (amplification data point: temperature)
data.adp.tmp.descr: Temperature in degrees Celsius at the time of measurement (optional) for an amplification data point.
data.adp.tmp.evidence: Temperature - The temperature in degrees Celsius at the time of measurement.

data.adp.fluor.name: adp.fluor (amplification data point: fluorescence)
data.adp.fluor.descr: Fluorescence intensity measured for an amplification data point (raw fluorescence, not baseline-corrected).

data.mdp.tmp.name: mdp.tmp (melting data point: temperature)
data.mdp.tmp.descr: Temperature for a melting-curve data point (part of dpMeltingCurveType).
data.mdp.tmp.evidence: Melting curve data point - The single data points measured in the melting analysis. (and dpMeltingCurveType tmp documentation: Temperature - The temperature in degrees Celsius at the time of measurement.)

dataCollectionSoftware.name_version.name: dataCollectionSoftware (name + version)
dataCollectionSoftware.name_version.descr: Software name and version used to collect and/or analyze the data (dataCollectionSoftwareType).
dataCollectionSoftware.name_version.evidence: Software name and version used to collect and analyze the data.

experiment.run.react.structure_note.name: experiment/run/react structure (note)
experiment.run.react.structure_note.descr: RDML organizes experiments containing runs; runs contain reactions (react), which reference samples and contain data vectors. This hierarchical structure is used repeatedly in the docs and tools.
experiment.run.react.structure_note.evidence: An experiment can contain several runs. A run is a set of reactions performed in one "run", for example one plate, one rotor, one array, one chip. ... In a final RDML file, for example, one target might be referenced many times.

raw_full_info.source: RDML-Edit / RDML-Tools documentation and RDML package vignettes
raw_full_info.quote_location: RDML-Edit / Experiment description and RDML package docs

standards.notes: This extraction selects representative top-level elements and frequently used data fields from the RDML XSD and documentation (v1.0–v1.2 materials and package docs). The RDML schema is extensive; the full XSD lists many additional element types and attributes (e.g. targetType sequences, commercialAssay, templateQuantity, thermalCyclingConditions, pcrFormatType, quantityType enumerations). Each field above is supported by a verbatim quote from the provided source material.
